name: Samuel L. Jackson
current_role: Actor and producer; starring in Paramount+'s Tulsa King spin-off 'Frisco King' (2026)
profile: Washington D.C.-born, Chattanooga-raised actor, among the highest-grossing film actors ever (Pulp Fiction, Star Wars prequels, Marvel's Nick Fury). Wealth comes from a five-decade film career; received an Academy Honorary Award in 2022. Currently leading the Tulsa King spin-off Frisco King and producing a live-action Afro Samurai film.
interesting_fact: An avid golfer, Jackson has had a clause in his film contracts allowing him to play golf during shoots.
deep_cut_fact: Before his breakthrough he worked as an overnight security guard at the Manhattan Plaza apartment complex in New York; at Morehouse he started as a marine-biology major and was a cheerleader. In 2019 he was granted Gabonese citizenship after a DNA test linked him to Gabon's Benga people.
notes: Hollywood star, not an entrepreneur/energy figure; outreach would realistically go via his talent agency/publicist (not found published here). Wikipedia rate-limited; contacts are his long-standing verified social accounts.

name: Beth Wozniak
current_role: Chair & CEO, nVent Electric plc; director, Parker-Hannifin
profile: Canadian-born engineer who spent ~25 years at Honeywell (aerospace, automation & controls) before joining Pentair in 2015 and becoming the inaugural CEO of nVent at its 2018 spin-off. She has repositioned nVent around electrical connection/protection and AI data-center liquid cooling, where it has deployed 2+ GW and keeps adding US capacity.
interesting_fact: Under Wozniak nVent leased a 160,000 sq ft site in Blaine, Minnesota (announced July 2026) - its third data-center liquid-cooling capacity expansion in three years - and is supplying rack-level cooling for AMD's Helios AI platform.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in southern Ontario, she swam on her high-school team, studied engineering physics at McMaster, and started at Honeywell in Toronto before postings in Montreal and Phoenix; on data-center cooling she has summed it up as 'Heat is the enemy of electronics.' She has chaired NEMA's Board of Governors since 2024.

public_contacts.value: Kevin.King@nVent.com (Kevin H. King, VP Global Communications)

notes: Highly relevant guest for a data-center/energy podcast (liquid cooling, power distribution for AI). Best route: nVent global communications.

name: Mohan Anand Chandavarkar
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, FDC Limited (Mumbai) since 1 April 2026
profile: Second-generation leader of FDC Limited, the Mumbai drugmaker his father Anand Chandavarkar started as Fairdeal Corporation (incorporated 1940) to import and distribute medicines and infant foods. FDC makes ~147 brands across anti-infectives, gastro, ophthalmology and more, and is best known for Electral oral rehydration salts. Long-time MD, he was re-designated Chairman & MD in April 2026.
interesting_fact: FDC began as an importer/distributor (Fairdeal Corporation) of drugs, infant foods and surgical appliances before turning manufacturer; its Electral ORS is one of India's best-known rehydration brands.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal social accounts found. Route via company secretarial/investor desk (Mumbai, tel published on filings). Pharma, not energy/data-center.

name: Li Nanjing
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder of Kingfa Sci. & Tech. Co., Ltd. (SSE: 600143), Guangzhou; former general manager
profile: Li Nanjing (李南京) is one of the early partners of Kingfa Sci. & Tech., founded in Guangzhou in 1993 and now one of the world's largest modified-plastics makers (engineering, recycled and biodegradable plastics, carbon-fibre composites). He remains a top-10 shareholder with ~91.8 million tradable A-shares. Founder/controlling holder Yuan Zhimin and chairman Chen Pingxu are the company's public faces.
interesting_fact: Kingfa grew from a 1993 Guangzhou start-up into a global modified-plastics leader and has expanded upstream into petrochemicals, announcing a ~US$1.5bn petrochemical plant investment.
notes: Very private; no interviews found. The SEC field linking him to Odyssey Therapeutics (ODTX) director looks like a name-match error - unverified, treat with caution. Shareholding confirmed on 10jqka top-holder list (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/144/600143/holder.html). Route via Kingfa board secretary/IR.

name: Luo Youcheng
current_role: Listed by source data as the owner of Jinduo Ceramics (Foshan Jinduo Ceramics Co., Ltd.), Foshan, Guangdong; current title not verified
profile: Luo Youcheng (罗有成) is listed as the source of wealth behind Jinduo Ceramics, a tile maker headquartered on Nanzhuang Avenue in Foshan's Chancheng district, China's ceramic-tile capital. The company makes porcelain floor and wall tiles in large formats up to 1200x2400 mm. Searches in English and Chinese found no further biographical detail.
interesting_fact: Jinduo is based in Foshan's Nanzhuang, the cluster that produces a large share of China's ceramic tiles; its range includes large slabs up to 1200x2400 mm.
notes: Very private, essentially no English or Chinese web presence found; identity/role could not be independently confirmed. Company publishes a general hotline on its site. Not energy/data-center related.

name: Irshad Mirza
profile: Kanpur leather industrialist, founder/executive chairman of Mirza International (RedTape footwear) and Padma Shri recipient (2010). Died 4 December 2022 in Kanpur.
notes: Deceased (4 Dec 2022), confirmed by ETV Bharat and Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irshad_Mirza). Family business continues: RedTape chairman is Rashid Ahmed Mirza (https://redtape.com/pages/chairs-man-massage).

name: Nicholas John Swenson
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Air T, Inc. (NASDAQ: AIRT); Chairman of Pro-Dex (PDEX); managing member of AO Partners / Groveland Capital
profile: Minneapolis value investor who runs Air T as a Berkshire-style holding company (FedEx feeder air cargo, Global Ground Support de-icers, aircraft parts, Delphax and more) since 2013. Through AO Partners/Groveland he is a 10%+ owner and chairman of Pro-Dex, an Irvine maker of powered surgical instruments, a position held since 2013.
interesting_fact: Air T describes itself as an 'industrious American holding company' with businesses spanning overnight air cargo for FedEx, aircraft de-icing equipment, regional airline and aircraft teardown/parts - and invites shareholders to submit questions to management via an open online Q&A.
deep_cut_fact: Before striking out on his own he spent roughly 2001-2009 as a portfolio manager and partner at Minneapolis hedge fund Whitebox Advisors, then founded Groveland Capital with a value-investing approach to hedged credit.

public_contacts.value: kphilp@airt.com (Katrina Philp, Chief of Staff - investor questions)

notes: Accessible, shareholder-friendly operator; best route is Air T chief of staff or inquiries@airt.com. Not energy-focused but a holding-company/capital-allocation guest.

name: Luis A Gonzalez
current_role: Director and 10%+ shareholder, Mission Produce, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVO)
profile: Peruvian agribusiness entrepreneur who founded Camposol (Peru's leading agro-industrial company and once the world's largest asparagus exporter) and Austral Group, Peru's second-largest fishing/marine food producer. He co-founded avocado grower Grupo Arato in 2011, which Mission Produce acquired in 2018; he has sat on Mission's board since around 2011.
interesting_fact: He helped pioneer Peru's avocado export boom: as head of Camposol he had already planted a 900-hectare avocado test plot before the industry took off, and Peruvian farms now supply a large share of Mission's avocados.
deep_cut_fact: Before avocados, he built businesses in two very different Peruvian sectors - asparagus (Camposol became the world's largest asparagus exporter) and fishing/marine foods (Austral Group).

public_contacts.value: apearson@missionproduce.com (Andrew Pearson, VP Investor Relations & Strategy)

notes: Private, Lima-based; no personal social accounts or interviews found. Only route found is via Mission Produce press/IR. Name is common - identity tied to Mission board bio.

name: Xu Xinxi
current_role: Listed by source data as the owner behind Zhaoshan Xinxing Group (兆山新星集团), a Zhejiang cement group; current title not verified
profile: Xu Xinxi (徐新喜) is listed as deriving his wealth from Zhaoshan Xinxing Group, a Zhejiang building-materials/cement group that in 2005 began a 1.35bn-yuan cement plant in Liuyang, Hunan. Searches in English and Chinese found no biography or public statements, and one investor-database profile names other executives (Huang Zhaoshan, Huang Xinhua), so his role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Zhejiang Zhaoshan Xinxing Group started building a 1.35bn yuan (~US$163m) cement plant in Liuyang, Hunan, on 7 March 2005.
notes: Very private / near-zero web footprint; identity and link to the group unverified. Group website (zsxx-group.com) was unreachable. Recommend checking Qichacha/Tianyancha registry data before outreach.

name: John D Idol
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Capri Holdings (Michael Kors, Jimmy Choo) - stepping down 4 Jan 2027, then senior adviser to 31 Mar 2027
profile: Fashion executive who held senior roles at Ralph Lauren (mid-1990s) and ran Donna Karan (1997-2001) before buying Michael Kors in 2003 with Sportswear Holdings for ~$100m when revenue was ~$20m. He built it into Capri Holdings (adding Jimmy Choo and Versace, later sold to Prada in 2025). In Nov 2026 Capri named Justin Boxford to succeed him as CEO.
interesting_fact: He and his partners bought Michael Kors for about $100 million in 2003 when the label had roughly $20 million in revenue, then took it public in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: In 2018 he was part of the Lawrence Stroll-led consortium that bought the Force India Formula One team - the team that became today's Aston Martin F1 team.
notes: Transitioning out of Capri (succession announced ~12 Nov 2026: https://fashionunited.com/news/people/capri-holdings-appoints-justin-boxford-as-ceo-john-idol-prepares-to-retire/2026111175694); may be more available for interviews after Q1 2027. No personal social accounts found.

name: John R. Furner
current_role: President & CEO, Walmart Inc. (succeeded Doug McMillon in 2026)
profile: Arkansas-raised Walmart lifer who started in 1993 as a part-time hourly associate and rose through buying, store and district management. He ran Sam's Club (2017-2019) and Walmart U.S. (2019-2026) before becoming CEO of Walmart Inc. in 2026, steering its omnichannel, automation and AI push.
interesting_fact: By age 31 he had gone from hourly associate to assistant store manager, assistant buyer, store manager, district manager and buyer - a path he called 'an amazing ride'.
deep_cut_fact: His first Walmart job was in the garden center of Store 100 in Bentonville, Arkansas, in 1993; he went back to Store 100 on his first day as Sam's Club CEO. Raised in Jacksonville, Arkansas, he studied marketing management at the University of Arkansas's Sam M. Walton College of Business.
notes: Very high-demand CEO; requests must go through Walmart Global Communications media-relations form. Angle for podcast: Walmart's energy/renewables and store/DC automation.

name: William L Meaney
current_role: President & CEO, Iron Mountain (NYSE: IRM); director, State Street Corp.
profile: New Hampshire-born engineer (RPI) and Carnegie Mellon Tepper MSIA (1986) who did turnarounds at South African Airways and Swiss International Air Lines, then tripled sales at Hong Kong's Zuellig Group as its first non-family CEO. Since 2013 he has transformed Iron Mountain from records storage into a fast-growing data-center, digital and asset-lifecycle business.
interesting_fact: Under Meaney, Iron Mountain's data-center, digital and asset-lifecycle businesses collectively grew more than 40% in 2025, and the company entered 2026 on the back of strong data-center leasing.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he worked summer jobs for the Morrell family at Story Land, the New Hampshire theme park - an experience he lists among the four that shaped him. He tells his team to 'become comfortable being uncomfortable' and likens international business to 'three-dimensional versus two-dimensional chess'.
notes: Top-priority fit for a data-center podcast (Iron Mountain Data Centers is a major colocation/hyperscale developer). Route via media@ironmountain.com.
